plan.summary: Add a REVERSE movement order that moves a vehicle exactly one grid cell opposite its current orientation without changing that orientation, while preserving existing boundary and simultaneous-collision behavior.
steps: Add REVERSE to MovementOrder so turns can express backward movement.
Add a Direction operation that returns the opposite direction for NORTH, EAST, SOUTH, and WEST, replacing or correcting the currently unused modeForward helper as appropriate.
Handle REVERSE in MovementEngine.applyOrder by moving the position one cell in the direction opposite the vehicle orientation while retaining the original orientation.

Reuse the existing board validation and conflict-resolution pipeline so reverse moves are blocked at board boundaries and participate identically in target collisions, swaps, vacated-position chains, and stationary-vehicle blocking.

Update the game rules to define the reverse movement vectors and orientation behavior, apply boundary and collision rules to reverse movement, add REVERSE to the supported orders, and remove reverse movement from the out-of-scope list.
tests: Add parameterized or equivalent unit coverage proving REVERSE moves one cell backward for all four orientations and leaves orientation unchanged.
Add a unit test proving a reverse move outside the board is blocked.
Add reverse-specific collision coverage, including reversing into a stationary vehicle and a conflict involving simultaneous forward and reverse movement.
Run the backend test suite with ./mvnw test from the backend directory to verify the new behavior and existing movement rules.
